mission: The galley. Sera sets down her fork with precision that is itself a warning. Torin puts reasonable hands on the table. Four positions surface — Sera's, Torin's, Kael's, and Ben's (absent). Ben tables the debate; Kael closes it with a line that no one has an answer to.
why_now: The thinning in the previous scene pushed the underlying disagreement into the room. Proceed without naming the positions and the group fractures on the next Corridor stop instead of at a table.
conflict: Three irreconcilable readings of the same history. Sera treats the lattice as something sacred and the technique as a violation. Torin treats the lattice as structure and the technique as a tool. Kael treats both frameworks as institutional propaganda. Ben does not have a position, and that is the problem.
turning_point: Kael speaks last. 'You're all arguing about whose cage has nicer bars.' Nobody answers, because nobody has a good answer.
opening_hook: It starts over food. Torin says something about the technique that makes Sera put down her fork with precision that is itself a warning.
closing_hook: Kael speaks last, after everyone else has committed: 'You're all arguing about whose cage has nicer bars.' Nobody answers. Because nobody has a good response.
emotional_trajectory: Simmering tension -> heated philosophical collision -> uncomfortable silence

stakes.personal: Ben's worldview destabilising — the Force he was taught does not match the room he is standing in
stakes.interpersonal: The group's ideological fault lines exposed
stakes.external: Their ability to act together depends on some resolution or at least coexistence

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cramped common area, everyone too close together
sensory_details: Food cooling on plates; Sera's diction sharpening; Torin's warmth thinning for the first time in front of all of them; Kael's voice flat and cutting; Desh watching from the galley like an intelligence analyst reading a room
action_beats: Sera puts down her fork with controlled precision when Torin raises the technique over their meal
Torin spreads his hands on the table — a gesture of measured reasonableness that makes his argument feel inevitable
Kael speaks last, his words landing in the silence after everyone else has committed their positions
promises_planted: Three different Force traditions can work in concert (PP13)
notes: Veraine's position (lattice as disease) is present by absence — the missing fourth voice, audible in its shape around the three that speak. Kael's 'whose cage has nicer bars' is the line readers should remember from this chapter — plant it and leave. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, internally synthesise all four positions into a framework. He is the one person at the table without a settled answer; the scene's value is that his not-knowing is visible through what he does not say, not through an interior monologue labelling his own destabilisation. Anti-patterns: no monologues; Torin's reasonableness must be genuinely compelling on the page, not a strawman; Sera's anger should register in posture and diction, not in a speech.
